title: Alignment strawman prep: product + eng + applied-ml
body:
Context: prepping a lightweight alignment sync between Product (hosted API + console), Serving Runtime (eng), and Applied ML to converge on priorities for H2 roadmap and early 2027 bets. This is a personal scratchpad / strawman to bring to the meeting. Goal is to leave with 3 prioritized bet areas, clear owners, and a short list of blockers to unblock before the next review.

Meeting logistics
- Target: 45 minutes (tight) + 15 min async follow-up window
- Proposed attendees (core): Hannah (Product), Marco (Eng - serving runtime), Lina (Applied ML), Arjun (Product PM - dedicated), optional: Priya (Console), Dev (SRE)
- Date/time: Thu 2026-04-15 10:00-11:00 PT
- Prep asks: owners flagged in "prep tasks" below to bring a single slide / 3 bullets.

Meeting objectives (top-level)
1) Agree on top 3 cross-team roadmap priorities for H2 (not full roadmap, but crosscutting bets we must coordinate on).
2) Surface critical dependencies (infra, model-ops, quantization tooling) and assign unblock owners.
3) Sync on measurable success metrics for each priority and how we'll eval regressions (who owns eval sets).

Proposed agenda (45m)
- 0-5m: quick context + proposed prioritization criteria (impact, unblockability, revenue/ops risk)
- 5-20m: strawman presentation (Hannah) — 3 cross-team bets with rationale (5m each)
- 20-35m: focused discussion on dependencies & timeline compression options
- 35-42m: owners, success metrics, and immediate blockers
- 42-45m: confirm next check-in cadence + quick retro note

Strawman: top 3 cross-team bets (brief)
1) Low-latency fallback routing for high-value hosted API customers
- Why: reduce P50 P95 tail spikes during model overloads; keep SLAs for paid tiers.
- Key work: policy routing + automatic model-variant fallback, canary rollout in console, observability hooks in console and tracing.
- Rough timeline: prototype Q3 start, canary Q3 end, GA early Q4.
- Owners: Marco (runtime routing implementation), Arjun (product rollout policy), Lina (validate output parity on fallback models).
- Success metrics: reduce SLA violations by 75% under overload tests; maintain quality regression < 2% on eval prompts.

2) Model quantization and inference-cost playbook for Dedicated customers
- Why: Dedicated customers demand predictable cost; quantization can materially cut GPU utilization if we standardize profiles.
- Key work: define quantization profiles, integrate into model onboarding pipeline, add guidance to console optimize recommendations.
- Timeline: profile experiments Q2-Q3; integrate pipeline and docs Q4.
- Owners: Lina (quant experiments), Marco (runtime kernel fallbacks + accuracy monitoring), Priya (console docs + UX).
- Success metrics: 20-40% reduce GPU vCPU usage on targeted models; documented per-model cost delta in console.

3) Shared eval set + regression alerting for feature rollouts (prompt-set driven)
- Why: avoid surprises when switching model versions or enabling new optimizations (kv caching, batching changes).
- Key work: canonical eval set, regression thresholds, CI hooks for model deploys, alerting/rollback integration in Console.
- Timeline: canonicalization and infra Q3, CI integration Q4.
- Owners: Lina (eval & thresholds), Marco (CI + runtime hooks), Hannah/Arjun (policy on rollbacks).
- Success metrics: no post-deploy quality regression > 3% on canonical set; auto-fallback triggers during detected regressions.

Risks & unknowns
- Model parity when routing to quantized variants — need more head-to-head test cases (Lina to run).
- Capacity planning for low-latency fallbacks may require extra Dedicated pools or burst strategy — cost modeling needed (Finance).
- Console UX complexity: exposing too many knobs confuses customers; need product constraints.
- Data privacy/regulatory constraints for Private customers when collecting eval prompts for canonical set.

Prep tasks (who brings what)
- Hannah: 3-slide strawman distilled to 3 bullets each bet + prioritization criteria. (Due: Tue 4/14)
- Marco: short perf sketch on routing architecture options + rough infra cost delta for fallback pools. Link INF-4823. (Due: Wed 4/14)
- Lina: preliminary eval snippets showing parity for quantized variants + list of missing testcases. (Due: Wed 4/14)
- Arjun: customer signals / revenue impact summary for SLA violations (2 top customers impacted). (Due: Wed 4/14)
- Priya (optional): how these features might surface in Console; 1 UX risk slide.

Action item template (to confirm in meeting)
- Action: <short description> | Owner: <name> | Due: <YYYY-MM-DD> | Acceptance: <metric/artefact>
- Pre-fill candidates:
  - Action: Run parity eval between base model and quantized-8bit profile on canonical eval set | Owner: Lina | Due: 2026-05-08 | Acceptance: delta < 2% on quality metrics
  - Action: Prototype fallback router POC + load test | Owner: Marco | Due: 2026-07-01 | Acceptance: P95 during overload within SLA target

Open questions to surface in meeting
- Is Finance comfortable with estimated cost to reserve fallback capacity or should we prioritize purely software fallbacks first? (Ping: Finance lead: Priya G.)
- For canonical eval set, can we share prompts across Hosted customers or must we stitch synthetic/bench prompts to avoid PII?
- Rollout policy: do we prefer automatic fallback + rollback vs manual A/B gating for first 3 customers?

Notes to self (talking points)
- Emphasize product risk: customer-facing outages lead to churn; framing decisions around concrete SLOs helps.
- Avoid getting lost in low-level infra details in first sync; capture blockers and owners, then schedule deep-tech follow-ups.
- Keep measurement focus: push for one unified eval pipeline owned by Applied ML.

Post-meeting follow-ups (template)
- Send concise notes + action table within 24h.
- Owners drop one-line weekly status into shared Confluence card (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Crossfunc+Roadmap)
- Schedule next sync: 3 weeks cadence until alignment complete, then monthly.

Quick references (tickets / docs to mention)
- JIRA: INF-4823 (routing prototype)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/2218 (batching + routing hooks)
- Confluence: Model Onboarding Checklist + Eval standards (link above)
- Slack threads: #aml-roadmap, #hosting-ops

Misc scratch (do not bring to meeting unless asked)
- Idea: small external beta with 2 high-value customers to validate fallback UX + billing model (metered vs reserved).
- Consider running a tabletop incident drill with fallback active to validate observable signals and runbook clarity.

End of scratchpad. Will prune to 1 slide per bet and 1 slide for dependencies before meeting.
